# SealQL

Everything an application developer or AI needs is in `examples/`: concepts and rules first, then one folder per adapter with a guide and compilable code.

## Reading order

1. `examples/README.md` — keys, field/search choices, leakage, scopes, budgets, and rebuild order.
2. Choose a supported adapter:
   - Drizzle ORM 0.45: `examples/drizzle/v0.45/README.md` (guide) and the code next to it; export `sealql/drizzle/v0.45`.
3. For core-only field encryption, use export `sealql` and `examples/core/sealer.ts`. Database search lifecycle is adapter-owned.
4. For implemented internals and the security boundary, see the repository docs: https://github.com/jmp-develop/sealql/blob/main/docs/current-state.md and https://github.com/jmp-develop/sealql/blob/main/docs/threat-model.md.

## Non-negotiable constraints

- `standard` is the only product search design. Do not present rejected stateful, posting-page, or bucket research as product behavior.
- Keys are fixed global or model keys. There is no key version, in-place rotation, user/group key, or database policy table.
- Substring search and each LIKE literal run require at least two normalized characters. Encrypted range, sort, aggregate, exact statistics, and standalone one-character substring search are unsupported.
- Warning: ordinary substring tokens on fixed-format, small-alphabet fields such as phone or account numbers let an attacker with known values assemble unseen values; prefer exact search or use `hardened: true` for partial lookup. Ordinary exact search still leaks equality and frequency.
- Field option `hardened: true` omits deterministic candidate tokens and uses salted proofs with the same query API; use it only where token leakage matters, search work can grow with scope size and be tens to hundreds of times slower (the initial sweep reached about 160× overall at 100,000 rows and about 8–40× in some 10,000-row cases; https://github.com/jmp-develop/sealql/blob/main/bench/results/2026-10-02-hardened/perf/report-ko.md), and combine other indexed conditions on large scopes. Lists with few matches can still be slower than count; see https://github.com/jmp-develop/sealql/blob/main/bench/results/2026-10-02-hardened/list-plan/report-ko.md. Query observation and parameter logs expose the same query-key leakage as ordinary substring search; enabling or disabling it requires migration → `extraMigrationSql` → `prepareAllSearch`.
- Hardened removes stored candidate-token determinism only; query parameters still carry value-specific keys, so bind-parameter logging must remain disabled. Existing-field conversions also require companion rewriting or recreation while pre-transition backups/WAL archives retain old tokens: discard them if all retained data must have the token-free hardened guarantee, or protect retained copies under the original profile's security controls; see the adapter's migration guide.
- Managed writes and the documented migration → `extraMigrationSql` → `prepareAllSearch` → query deployment order prevent silent search omissions.
- `count` returns one exact safe `number`; a budget or safe-integer overflow is an error. Search has no implicit work ceiling, so applications set budgets from measurements.
- Use `sealed.where` for verified encrypted predicates inside caller-owned Drizzle JOINs, subqueries, ordering, and counts; reserve `sealed.search` for SealQL-managed cursor paging and candidate-shape checks.
- After migrations and `extraMigrationSql`, use top-level `prepareAllSearch` as the offline all-registered-model catalog, reindex, and coverage gate before deploying new search code.
